content.text: No audit or inspection right over our usage exists anywhere in the agreement — searches for "audit," "inspect," "records," "verif," and "monitor" returned nothing, and the fee, license, and Client covenant sections contain no verification right.

input.quote: Client will be provided upon request with documentation supporting the amount charged
input.rationale: The Agreement grants TrueLink no audit, inspection, or usage-verification right against Mortgage Logic.com. Searches for "audit," "inspect," "records," "verif," and "monitor" return no hits, and the sections where such rights would sit contain none: § 5–6 (Compensation / Documentation and Disputes) runs the other way, giving Client the right to documentation supporting charges and to contest them; § 8 (Covenants and Warranties of Client) imposes only compliance, access-restriction and content warranties; § 2–3 give Client (not TrueLink) access to Interface usage statistics and raw log files (p0037). The only TrueLink self-help right, § 8(f) (p0058), permits TrueLink to implement technical mechanisms on its own hosted platform to prevent spamming or illegal activity — it is not an audit right and confers no access to Client systems or records. Because the absence of any Customer-side audit right is more favorable than our preferred position (annual, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, Vendor cost, no system access), no redline is warranted; we should simply resist any audit right being added in negotiation.
